Vision, purpose & values
Within our #KemnalSchools, the shared and common purpose is to work together as a community of schools to ensure that every child, whatever their background, receives a high quality education.
The Kemnal Academies Trust is one of the largest Multi-Academy Trusts in the South and East of England with 45 Special, Primary, Secondary and All Through Academies.
Welcome to The Kemnal Academies Trust
The Kemnal Academies Trust is one of the largest Multi-Academy Trusts in the South and East of England with 45 Special, Primary, Secondary and All Through Academies.
You can find out more on our trust website.
Ambition for every child. Pride in the communities we serve.
We are a group of schools with ambition for every child and pride in the communities we serve.
We provide a broad and rich education that opens doors. Working together, we give every pupil the start they need to build a life of purpose and contribution.
TKAT ACE programme
One of our priorities is to support pupils most in need. TKAT ACE - a champion for every child - plays a key role in that. This is a unique and innovative pastoral mentoring programme that provides a dedicated and specially trained 1:1 tutor for disadvantaged pupils and their families. The aim is to help these pupils overcome barriers to their progress both in terms of academic outcomes, and their social and emotional development.
You can find out more on the TKAT ACE area.
Train to teach with Kemnal
The Kemnal Academies Trust, SCITT Teacher Training scheme is a highly successful school-based Initial Teacher Training programme.
We offer high quality training through our partnership of primary and secondary schools in the South and East of England. You can find out more on our TKAT SCITT website.
Careers at Kemnal
At The Kemnal Academies Trust, we believe that through the recruitment and development of committed and passionate colleagues, we can continue to deliver great outcomes for our pupils.
Our high quality professional development pathways support and empower all our staff at all stages of their career, and promote a culture of continuous learning, innovation and knowledge sharing. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice.
We provide a climate where our staff feel valued, where they have a voice that is heard, where they can develop to be the best versions of themselves and progress within our Trust.
You can find out more on our TKAT careers site.
Contact The Kemnal Academies Trust
Address: The Kemnal Academies Trust, The Atkins Centre, Kemnal Technology College, Sevenoaks Way, Kent DA14 5AA
Telephone: 020 3740 1808
Email: enquiries@tkat.org

Personal Data
Use of photographs and video
This guidance covers photos or video (images) of people taken for School purposes.
If the image can be used to identify an individual and tell you something about them it is likely that it will be personal data for the purpose of the Data Protection Act. People can obviously be identified from names but may also be identified from contextual information e.g. the caption reads: ‘This photo shows students working in the school library’.
The following examples will help you to identify the issues that you need to consider.
Photos of specific individuals/groups
Where an image is clearly of an individual or group of individuals, who are the focus of the image, it will be personal data, and consent is required to use it. Although the Data Protection Act does not specify that consent should be in written form it is strongly recommended that you obtain written consent so that you have a record, in case of subsequent disputes.
Photos where individuals inadvertently appear in the background
It will not normally be necessary to obtain the specific permission of all who appear incidentally in the background of publicity shots where they are clearly not the focus of the image.
Photos of large crowds/events
Where an image does not focus on one individual or group of individuals, the data is unlikely to be personal data. In addition, it may not be practicable to obtain the consent of every individual. However, it is good practice to ensure that there are clear signs around the venue indicating that publicity photos are being taken.
Publishing an image on the web is a potential disclosure to the world at large. Particular care must be taken therefore to obtain appropriate consent where the image constitutes personal data. In cases of doubt you should err on the side of caution and not publish the image.
It may not be appropriate to ask VIPs to complete consent forms, in which case it should be sufficient to obtain verbal consent.
Although the Data Protection Act does not specify an age limit where images of children are being taken it is important to obtain written consent from the child’s parent/guardian.
If your child is under the age of 13, please complete this form. For children over the age of 13, the form will be completed by the student in school.
If you wish to withdraw consent, please complete this form

Adverse Weather Conditions
The decision to close the school will be made by the Headteacher, who will make a judgement if any one or more of the following conditions apply:
There are not enough staff who are able to get to school to keep the school running safely
Conditions on the school site/campus are too dangerous
Conditions are considered to be or are anticipated to become too hazardous for students and staff later in the day.
The front page of our website will have the latest information on whether the school is open, closed, closing due to an emergency situation or open only to certain year groups on a particular school day. It will also have instructions for any students due to take public exams and may have instructions to particular year groups about school work.
A decision to close the school or send students home early is always very difficult. Careful consideration is always given to the latest local weather reports, information about road conditions, bus and train services and the safety of the school site.
Additional information may be available on local radio and the West Sussex website but please be aware, they do not always have the latest information. It is always best to check the school website first.
If the school has to close early due to severe weather conditions, we will ensure that your child has contacted you and that you know where they are going once they leave the school site. They will be asked to sign against their name on a register to confirm that they have contacted you and made arrangements. They will be told to come back into school if their bus or train is cancelled when they get to the bus or train station.
We will inform students of any changes to normal bus and train arrangements so they can inform you. Students who have been unable to contact parents/guardians will be kept safe and supervised until contact has been made and permission has been given to let them leave the site. The school will remain open until the last student has left the site.
